locations.name: Kest Depot
locations.ownership: Privately operated by Gilt Ledger; Reedbank remains independent.
locations.history: The building began as a raised freight store serving ferry traffic. Veyra’s business made its reliable handling a public reputation and its selective access a source of power. Flood marks on the outer steps record maintenance, not supernatural immunity. The refuge and public charter records elsewhere in Reedbank are not owned by the depot.
locations.daily_life: Bale compares a physical count to the day’s dispatch instructions. Legitimate customers collect orders while disputed allocations wait in a marked side bay. Workers use both large wagon doors; no stack occupies the six-metre freight aisle. Veyra meets difficult visitors on the floor when she wants the available stock to speak for her.
locations.dramatic_use: A withheld crate can sit in full view. Suspense comes from knowing it could leave, not from finding a secret chamber. The marked hold bay changes only through a documented order, making a worker’s refusal or release visible to witnesses.

locations.name: Slate Arcade Rooms
locations.ownership: Ordinary lodging business; a temporary Glass Thread lease does not implicate the landlord or other guests.
locations.history: This is a new name for the existing EXT-03-U04 lodging building, fifty metres east and one hundred north of Latchford’s civic origin. Its trade is rooms for crews in transit. Glass Thread uses one upper guest room during a later story, then moves on. The public North Relay Rooms remain a separate legitimate institution.
locations.daily_life: Guests share the ordinary stair passage and washing facilities. In Guest E, a folding cot, document table and portable repair bench make a rented room serve two purposes. Travel bags can be packed quickly because this is a temporary stay, not an underground headquarters. Quiet maintenance is possible; industrial work and permanent aerials are not added.
locations.dramatic_use: A lease date and a witness can establish presence without proving every act of the tenant. An unrelated guest’s complaint about noise matters more than a theatrical hidden emblem. The crew’s departure changes occupancy and prop state, not the town plan.

locations.name: Salt Crown Counting House
locations.ownership: Kavar’s accounts business; not owner of every public well.
locations.history: The counting house gained standing by making water claims easier to compare. Public counters and carefully maintained measures still perform useful work. Kavar exploited that trust by treating his certificate as the necessary condition of access and concealing the decision to keep a competing pump closed.
locations.daily_life: Claimants wait in the public reading room. Dispatch staff compare deliveries with accounts. Original files and private customer information remain in distinct archive rooms; a claim of wrongdoing does not turn every personal record into a public exhibit. No machinery here can switch off the desert’s wells.
locations.dramatic_use: A polished measure can be honest while the account beside it is false. The scene turns when a service witness describes a repair that the dated record says never happened. Even after that proof, Maela must explain a genuine limit on extraction.

locations.name: Echo Archive Council Room
locations.ownership: Still Bell institution; divided between disclosure and concentrated authority.
locations.history: The council uses upper Catalog A for small hearings around movable furniture. This does not create a new wing or change the public ground floor developed in Living Places. The room holds records made by several generations, including people whose knowledge was careful and whose decisions were still self-serving.
locations.daily_life: Archivists bring only the required copies to a hearing. Insulated sample cases remain closed except during supervised examination. Most disagreement is about evidence and authority, not a contest of magical powers. A modern alteration can sit beside a reliable old observation without contaminating the entire collection.
locations.dramatic_use: Ysolde places the two versions side by side and discloses her own family’s benefit from closure. Ossa’s strongest response is a correct account of the actual danger. The room must accommodate both admissions at once.

locations.name: Ashmouth Freight Yard
locations.ownership: Riven Claw occupies a disused freight site; civilian Cinder Cuts is elsewhere.
locations.history: After freight was diverted, this loading terrace lost its regular traffic. It retains a refuge lodge and service approaches because those were useful before Brakka arrived. The band’s occupation turns a workplace into a coercive store without making its original builders or the neighboring population complicit.
locations.daily_life: Dreg keeps crates sorted by use and remembers which harness needs repair. The west approach admits wagons; the east route is a narrow foot path. A fenced gas trough stays outside the working court. Ashmaws follow heat plumes in the wider terrain; neither Brakka nor Dreg commands them.
locations.dramatic_use: The loading platform makes a public order visible. When Brakka demands spectacle and Dreg protects usable supplies, everyone on the floor sees the split. Escape follows the registered approaches; the shelter offers cover and rest, not a hidden passage to town.

locations.name: Blackwake Mooring
locations.ownership: Abandoned mooring occupied by Serik’s three-craft crew.
locations.history: The platform was built for regulated cargo transfer within a local liftstone field. Its counterweights and load rules are older than Serik’s claim to the place. His occupation gives him a berth and a stage; it does not give him ownership of the air routes or control over the field.
locations.daily_life: One main winch deck feeds three docking arms. The rear refuge lodge uses the existing two shelter bays as separate refuge cells. A short connector links it to the deck. Each craft has a finite load envelope and must be counted in the scene state: berthed, arriving or away. Three small craft cannot become an unseen reserve fleet.
locations.dramatic_use: Eri recognizes a routine loading limit that Serik is trying to conceal. The heroes free people by making a viable departure possible, not by cutting every support and hoping the platform floats anyway. Captives and cargo compete for capacity; useful evidence may have to be left behind.

geometry.name: Blackwake Mooring

locations.name: The Cut Span
locations.ownership: A genuinely closed crossing inspected by Still Bell and independent reviewers.
locations.history: The deliberate severing belongs to the historical response to the Severance. Ossa’s later forged prohibition is a separate act. The north and south inspection places allow evidence to be gathered without reopening the gap. The longer foot detour still takes two days and leaves this sheet.
locations.daily_life: Inspectors approach their own abutment, compare marks and stop at the guarded edge. Detached couplings are examined behind the north rail. The north refuge remains at its inherited position; a measured south inspection lodge completes the two-house description already established in the atlas.
locations.dramatic_use: Expose a false order beside a dangerous structure that deserves a truthful warning. A refusal to reconnect can be the responsible outcome even when the official who demanded it has lied. No visual hint should turn the gap into an easy leap for the heroes.

geometry.name: The Cut Span
geometry.notes: North and south abutments are separate; a safe foot detour takes two days and does not reconnect the span.
geometry.hazard: Real coupled resonance hazard and choirwraith territory beyond the marked ridge.
